reader.requirement: At --std 85 the REWRITE operand record-name-1 must be the name of a level-01 logical record of a file description entry in the File Section, written alone or qualified (e.g. by file-name), so a working-storage item, a subordinate item of a record, a reference-modified record, a sort-merge record, a file-name, an ambiguous unqualified name, and the 2002 FILE file-name-1 and RECORD-word forms are refused.

edition-consulted.switches: GateFilePhrase: REWRITE FILE file-name-1 (construct write-rewrite-file-phrase-2002) and the word RECORD after record-name (rewrite-record-word-2002) refused below 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the FILE file-name-1 alternative and the RECORD word are 2002 forms, refused at 85 (COBOL0900) and legal at 2023; the record-name identity check itself is the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb347_record_name_identity is a RELEASE case sharing ResolveRecordName; REWRITE's own refusal arms (working-storage, subordinate, ref-modified, sort record, file-name, qualification) and the 85 edition arms are not exercised by it

probes.expected: REWRITE REC OF F1 (sequential) and REWRITE REC IN F2 FROM WS (relative, sequential access) with the same record-name under two FDs, each qualified by its file-name, replace the records read

probes.printed: error COBOL1757: REWRITE 'WS' ... 'WS' is not a logical record of any file description entry
error COBOL1757: ... 'KOFRECOFF1' is subordinate to 'REC', which is the logical record of 'F1'
error COBOL1757: ... record-name-1 is a record-name, not an identifier, so it shall not be reference-modified
error COBOL1692: REWRITE may not name the sort-merge file 'S1'
error COBOL1639: 'REC' does not uniquely identify a data item
error COBOL1639: 'F1' is declared as a file-name ... not as a data item
probes.expected: file-name in the record-name position refused

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the FILE phrase of a WRITE or REWRITE statement requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: REWRITE FILE F1 is not a 1985 format

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: the word RECORD after the record-name of a REWRITE statement requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: REWRITE REC OF F1 RECORD is not a 1985 format

reader.notes: ResolveRewriteRecord resolves the (qualified) reference and asks ResolveRecordName, whose identity test is FileModel.Records containment (level-01 of an FD, inherited GLOBAL FDs included), before the organization reroute, so sequential, relative and indexed REWRITE share it. Cosmetic: the subordinate-item message prints the qualified name without spaces ('KOFRECOFF1', rn.GetText()).

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: rw1 REWRITE R1 OF F2 (R1 belongs to F1) -> COBOL1639 not under qualifier F2; rw2 nested program REWRITE of a non-GLOBAL FD record of the container -> COBOL1639 not defined; rw3 CD record (Communication Section, a 1985-only section) -> COBOL1757 not a logical record of any FD; rw4 Linkage 01 -> COBOL1757; rw6 66 RENAMES RK THRU RV under an FD record -> COBOL1757 subordinate to R1; rw5 positive: second 01 of an FD (implicit redefinition) and REWRITE R1 IN F1 replace the records read, printed AAAXYZ / QQQQQQ.
